shortDescription: Ships a built-in resource pack that extends Fresh Animations to Quark's animals (currently the foxhound) and switches it on by itself when Quark and a Fresh Animations pack are both there.
oneLiner: Fresh Animations only covers vanilla mobs, so Quark's foxhound moves like stock Minecraft while every wolf beside it does not - this module carries a CEM pack that fills the gap and enables it automatically when Quark and a Fresh Animations pack are both installed.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: The animals the pack describes. Checked exactly, with ModList.get().isLoaded("quark") in QuarkFreshAnimationsPack#onAddPackFinders; without Quark the pack is never added, because assets/quark/optifine/cem/foxhound.jem would describe an entity that does not exist. No Quark type is named anywhere in the module - the class would otherwise fail verification on an installation without Quark (the beta.70 crash).

The reader. EMF is what interprets the pack's .jem geometry and .jpm expressions; it hooks EntityModelSet#bakeLayer generically, which is why a modded model works at all. Deliberately NOT part of the gate: without EMF the files are read by nobody - inert, not broken - so checking for it could only ever refuse wrongly.
optionalMods.evidence: resourcepacks/README.md; the pack lives at assets/quark/optifine/cem/, EMF's search path for a modded namespace

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddPackFindersEvent (mod bus, Dist.CLIENT, QuarkFreshAnimationsPack#onAddPackFinders - returns early unless the pack type is CLIENT_RESOURCES, the module is enabled, Quark is loaded and (unless require_fresh_animations is off) a Fresh Animations pack is found; then calls event.addPackFinders with alwaysActive=true and Pack.Position.TOP)

configKeys.effect: Only enable the built-in pack when a Fresh Animations pack is found in the game's resourcepacks folder. Unlike the Quark check this is a heuristic - Fresh Animations is a resource pack, not a mod, so there is no id to ask for and the file name is the only handle. The match strips everything but letters and lower-cases the rest, so FreshAnimations_v1.10.4.zip and fresh-animations both count. Turn it off when Fresh Animations lives somewhere the check cannot see (a modpack overlay, a renamed file), and the pack then enables itself on the Quark check alone.

notes:
WHAT THE PACK ACTUALLY CONTAINS
- resourcepacks/vpa_quark_fresh_animations/, shipped inside the jar by a processResources from-block in build.gradle (into 'resourcepacks', README.md excluded). Three files: foxhound.jem, foxhound_armor.jem and the shared foxhound_animations.jpm. The armour model is a SEPARATE baked model in Quark (quark:foxhound_armor, same mesh with sizeAdd 0.2), so it needs its own .jem - sharing the .jpm is what keeps animal and armour from drifting apart.
- The geometry was EXPORTED from EMF (models -> allmodels -> export), not typed out. In a .jem, "part": "head" is the key under which EMF replaces the original part; a wrong name fails SILENTLY - no error, no animation, no message.

WHY alwaysActive IS TRUE
- A resource pack added through AddPackFindersEvent is off by default (NeoForge's own javadoc says so), and a compatibility pack nobody switches on is a no-op. The off switch is therefore the module's enabled key, not the pack list. Consequence: the pack cannot be unticked in the resource pack screen while the module is on.

HOW THE OWNING JAR IS FOUND
- addPackFinders resolves its ResourceLocation's namespace as a mod id, and that id differs between the bundle (vanillaplusadditions) and the standalone jar (vpa_quark_fresh_animations). Rather than keep a list of names in sync with the build, locatePack() asks every loaded mod file which one actually carries resourcepacks/vpa_quark_fresh_animations and uses that mod's id.

ANIMATION DETAILS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE EDITING THE .jpm
- tx/ty/tz REPLACE a part's position, they do not offset it (EMF: EMFModelOrRenderVariable.TX writes ModelPart.x outright). Every such line must restate the part's own position before adding anything.
- invertAxis "xy" NEGATES translate x and y at load time (EMFPartData.prepare), so a part written as -2.5 in the .jem sits at +2.5 in ModelPart space. The .jem and the .jpm therefore speak different signs for the same part.
- At 20 tps anything above 10 Hz aliases into jitter. An early version of the sniffing ran at 23 Hz and looked broken for exactly that reason.
- Animation lines are evaluated in file order, so a var must be written before it is read. The file keeps its variables topologically sorted.
- The eyes compensate for a Quark quirk: its prepareMobModel puts the interest angle (player holding food) on the head's YAW axis where vanilla uses the ROLL axis, and setupAnim then adds the look direction on top, so the head turns up to 27 degrees past the player. var.head_off = head.ry - torad(head_yaw) is exactly that surplus and the pupils roll back by it.

RESTING POSE (source of a long misunderstanding)
- Quark's FoxhoundPlaceToRestGoal.canUse() requires isTame() && !isOrderedToSit() && !isResting(). The dog must be STANDING; ordering it to sit is what prevents it from lying down. Targets are LIT_FURNACE, FURNACE and GLOWING (any light-emitting non-fluid block, campfires included), and the block above the heat source must be empty.

SCOPE
- Only the foxhound so far. Crab, Stoneling, Wraith and the rest are files, not code: export, drop the .jem in beside this one, done.
